questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Ever since I was a child I have travelled a lot in Italy and my love for the country and the italian culture has grown bigger with time. Therefore I saw exchange as my chance to explore the italian culture more deeply. Also before exchange I started attending Italian language class which was also why I choose Italy to get a chance to improve my Italian.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Coming from a different system it was a bit confusing and overwhelming at the beginning to find the information I needed, however Massimo (exchange contact at La Statale) was and has been super helpful thoughout my exchange in Milano. He was very easy to get in contact with and get things done.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arriving in Milano Massimo helped us with the practical things connected to the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I began looking for housing in early spring and I think it took me two months finding the right place. I found my apartment on Spotahome which has many apartments or rooms avaible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Look up the neighborhoods and make sure that they are safe and starting looking for an apartment early. It can take time finding the right place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is a bit confusing with the information about which course you can take and which ones you can't. The information is not all at one place. I took me some time to figure the system out. Also getting the ECTS points to add up was a bit difficult but I think it is partly due to being used to another system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I tried surfing around on UNIMI's webpage and wrote to Massimo if I needed help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was one course that I couldn't get because it wasn't held anyway and then it took sometime to find a new course that could replace the course. So almost totally succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You must take your time to familiarize yourself with the website and how to find information. In addition, you should be aware that ECTS is different than at KU. In UNIMI the typical courses are 6 or 9 ECTS.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The bachelor courses at UNIMI are somewhat easier than those at KU, while the master courses at UNIMI are more comparable in difficulty to KU's bachelor courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is not the same amount of group work as at KU. It's more like being at a lecture.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Language of the Media
Journalism, Media and Politics
Human development and mobility in a changing world 
How to use international survey data for social research
World literatures in English

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. The professors were super proficient and the things taught in class were very interesting. Specially I liked Language of the Media because the professor was skilled communicator and made teaching very exciting by making it relatable to the students' lives.

questions.answer:

Housing was more expensive than I tought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can attend different types of team sports as the university and there are friday bars at some of the campus'.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try to go the the friday bars at the university. It is a nice way to meet local students and other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The trains run frequently and are not particularly expensive. Plus flixbus is also big in Italy. Therefore, I would recommend traveling around the country as much as possible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to start with, but I quickly learned that Italians take things at a different pace and their everyday life is put together differently than the Danes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to sit next to an Italian in class and talk to them during breaks. It is a chill way to get to know them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Italians are more chill and less stressed than Danes. They do things at a slightly different pace, which is healthy for Danes who are used to being bus.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Italians are better so seize the day than Danes, which is something many of us could learn something from.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take your time to familiarize yourself with their website.
Get used to things happening at a different pace.
Group teaching is more like a lectures.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I meet and shared a lovely and exciting time with.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring oout the educational system.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
